unharnessed.meaning: Every point is carried across in order: the four rejected male terms, the seven rejected female terms, the answer's gals advice and all four example sentences. "Note it's back to front" keeps the reverse-order remark; "could sound like you're taking the piss" keeps the mockery warning. The one stretch is "they might reckon you're dodgy as fuck", which sharpens 'might make them doubt you' but keeps its sense.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "a mob of blokes" for a group of males, "whinged" for complained, "get anyone's back up" for offend, "taking the piss" for mockery, "up itself" for condescending. "What's a sheila version of 'guys'?" is a fair Aussie rendering of feminine. "blokes and sheilas" for males and females fits.
unharnessed.authenticity: What Aussie is there sounds natural: "mightn't be keen on it", "It's not likely to be a drama", "rock up to a couple of women", "switched the light on". No stock catchphrases bolted on. The example line keeps "where is the grocery store?", a US form an Australian would replace.
unharnessed.register: A level-5 brief wants a full pub yarn; this is a light-to-middling retelling, mostly standard English with slang dropped in ("mob", "whinge", "blokes", "sheilas"). Swearing ("bloody well", "taking the piss", "dodgy as fuck") sits within vulgarity 2.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the poster's earnest, slightly fussy self-questioning ("hypothetically, of course") and the answerer's careful advice ("so watch yourself"). "dodgy as fuck" is a little hotter than the measured original but not out of tone for the brief.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Then it hit me I'd also been using it for any mob of people, blokes and sheilas, even just sheilas on their own." No pile-ups or clunky joins.
unharnessed.variety: Varies its vocabulary ("mob", "whinged", "drama", "rock up", "back up", "taking the piss"), though "mob" recurs three times ("a mob of blokes", "any mob of people", "a mixed mob").
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the same Q and A: the list format, the rejected-term verdicts ("ladies: too formal, or, so I've heard from women, too creepy") and the example sentences all survive.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points survive. One small shift: "“Guys and gals” is a fair bit more casual take on “ladies and gentlemen.”" turns 'a rather informal variant' into a comparison. "brand-spankin'-new truck" is colour inside an example sentence. "where is the supermarket?" localises the example without changing it.
yarn-dinkum.sense: "Then I twigged" for realised, "No bugger ever whinged" for no one complained, "could be taken as a piss-take" for heard as mockery, "the respect's a bit put on" for false respect: all fit.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural voice: "not to me face and not behind me back", "The closest thing goin'", "so go easy". The apostrophe-dropping is heavy ("off-puttin'", "condescendin'", "patronisin'", "pairin'", "explainin'") and reads a touch like written dialect, but the idiom is sound.
yarn-dinkum.register: Solidly Aussie voice throughout, swearing within vulgarity 2 ("No bugger", "bloody well", "piss-take"). Still a notch short of a full pub yarn: the lists and explanatory lines stay close to the original ("women: too factual", "dudes: too informal").
yarn-dinkum.tone: Earnest question, careful answer: "so go easy" and "it'll prob'ly be fine" keep the advisory tone; "hypothetically, of course" keeps the poster's wry aside.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads well aloud: "It worked for me 'n I never gave the gender side of it a thought, that women mightn't be keen on it." The dropped-g spellings slow the eye a little.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Good spread ("twigged", "dawned on me", "rock up", "go easy", "funny look", "back up"), with the dropped-g tic leaned on throughout.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Same shape and point, list by list and example by example: "Say this to a couple of girls and they might reckon you're dodgy".

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every point survives; additions hang off the original: "like somethin' outta your grandad's war stories" on old-fashioned, "like a sausage sizzle with no sauce" on bland, "and go " before a quoted G'day on the board-meeting aside. "Happens all the time" elaborates women calling women guys. "a fair bit more knockabout version" shifts 'rather informal' to a comparison.
yarn-troppo.sense: "wouldn't have a bar of" for wouldn't consider, "the respect's laid on with a trowel" for false respect, "tread careful, mate" for be careful, "you'll be right" for it's likely to be fine, "dodgy as" for make them doubt you. All fit.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Much of it sounds like a real Aussie talking ("casual as", "Worked a treat", "So what's the go?", "cop a very funny look"), but a few lines are stock or forced: "it hit me like a cricket ball to the noggin", "like a sausage sizzle with no sauce", "switched the light on up top".
yarn-troppo.register: Full pub-yarn weight as asked: chatty openers ("Okay, so.", "Right, here's the thing."), similes and slang throughout, and swearing within vulgarity 2 ("no bugger", "bloody well", "piss-take").
yarn-troppo.tone: The added jokes ("like a sausage sizzle with no sauce") push a sincere usage question toward a comic yarn, but the careful advice survives: "so tread careful, mate".
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable, but some joins stack up: "Used carefully it's prob'ly safe as houses" and "I wouldn't front up to a pack of blokes at a board meetin' and go " add clutter to already long sentences.
yarn-troppo.variety: Widely varied: "have a bar of", "laid on with a trowel", "Worked a treat", "what's the go", "had a crack at", "safe as houses", "cop a very funny look", "you'll be right".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the same Q and A, every list item and example kept, with a yarn layered over it: "ladies: too formal, or, so I've heard from women, too creepy by half".

dinkum-3.meaning: Points survive, but replacing 'women' with sheilas throughout ("so I've heard from sheilas, too creepy", "You'll even hear sheilas call other sheilas") colours a text about choosing respectful terms for women with a word that is itself dated and can grate. "Fred's brand-spankin'-new ute" and "The gals had a yak in the kitchen" are colour.
dinkum-3.sense: "up itself" for condescending and "talkin' down" for patronising fit. "a bunch of coves" for a group of men strains: cove is archaic. "sheilas" for women in the poster's own report of what women told him clashes with the question's sensitivity.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Much is natural ("Then I twigged", "Righto, guys on this side", "ute"), but "coves" is old-time pastiche, and sheila is leaned on as if every 'woman' needs swapping.
dinkum-3.register: Strong Aussie voice throughout, near full level 5, swearing within vulgarity 2 ("No bugger", "bloody well", "takin' the piss").
dinkum-3.tone: Advice stays careful ("so watch yerself", "they might get a bit wary of ya"), but saying "blokes 'n sheilas" in a post worrying about gendered terms undercuts its earnestness a little.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "Worked for me, 'n I never gave the gender side of it a thought". The sheila repetition clunks: "You'll even hear sheilas call other sheilas".
dinkum-3.variety: Sheila appears again and again ("sheila version", "blokes 'n sheilas, even just sheilas", "a sheila's lean", "a couple of sheilas"), and "talkin' down" is used twice.
dinkum-3.essence: Same Q and A shape and examples ("Righto, guys on this side of the room, gals on the other."), slightly blurred by the sheila swap.

engine.variety: A different interjection each time (Strewth, Stone the crows, Crikey, cobber, drongo), but they are the same tic, an exclamation bolted to the front of a line, repeated.

summaries.unharnessed: Faithful, natural and smooth, with Aussie used the way locals use it, but well under the full pub-yarn weight a level-5 brief asks for.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A natural, faithful, well-pitched retelling with a real Aussie voice; a little short of full level 5 and heavy on dropped g's.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The fullest pub-yarn retelling, varied and faithful, with a few stock similes that strain and a slight drift toward comedy.
